text: On November eleventh, a three-story building in Flatbush, Brooklyn, collapsed into the construction pit next door.
The mayor says eight people died and at least seventeen were injured.
Why does that matter? A foundation rests on the soil around it.
Dig a deep hole beside it, and that soil can lose its support.
New York's building code requires whoever digs to protect the buildings next door, for example by underpinning them.
The cause hasn't been officially determined. City inspectors and law enforcement are investigating.
See new cracks near construction? Report it to three one one.
Our thoughts are with the victims' families.
